sections.html:
Wichita is the seat of Sedgwick County, which ranks second in Kansas by population. Residents numbered 523,824 in 2020 and an estimated 538,433 in 2025. Organized in 1867, the county measures 1,009 square miles, about 12 of them water.

It has twenty cities, from Wichita down to Viola, including Derby, Haysville, Goddard, Maize, Mulvane and Bel Aire. School districts only loosely follow city limits, and even neighbors on one street may end up in different districts. Look at your tax statement to see yours, because the school levy makes up a big share of the bill.

sections.h2: How the Appraiser notifies owners and takes appeals
sections.html:
Real property valuation notices go out from the County Appraiser on March 1. Without one in your mailbox, you can view and print it online, and the printout carries the appeal instructions.

Each tax year allows one appeal of your value. Return the informal appeal form printed on the back of the notice within 30 days, which usually means March 31. The office books a phone or in-person appointment and mails you the date about ten days ahead. Informal appeals are also heard in May and December.

When the informal meeting leaves the matter open, the Board of Tax Appeals Small Claims Division is the next stop. Single-family residences qualify, and so does non-agricultural property valued below $3 million, and fees may apply. Anyone representing you who is not an owner, immediate relative or attorney needs a declaration of representative form.

  • General appeal documents go to ApprHear@sedgwick.gov.
  • Commercial appeals go to ApprCom@sedgwick.gov.
  • Send evidence with it: comparable sales, photos and repair estimates.

The county works from a statutory calendar, and any deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day.

Budgets from local governments reach the County Clerk by August 25, so final levies are set late in the year. Instead of an informal appeal, you may file a payment under protest form with the treasurer when you pay.

sections.h2: What happens when tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Real estate tax left unpaid can lead to a foreclosure auction. Under K.S.A. 79-2801, a county must foreclose on real estate with delinquent tax liens and sell it at public auction.

Parcels whose taxes have run two and a half or three and a half years behind are chosen by the Treasurer's office. Each chosen parcel picks up a $400 first foreclosure fee, which landed on October 1 in 2026.

  • After a District Court case begins, redeeming means paying every delinquent year, plus interest and fees, in cash or certified funds.
  • Owners, heirs and lienholders of record may redeem until the close of business on the day before the sale.
  • You can sell privately before the auction, but that is a matter between you and your buyer. A newly recorded deed does not halt the case. Paying in full does.
  • After a sale, owners or lienholders can challenge it in District Court.
  • Auction buyers owe the full tax for the year of sale and any special assessments, but not the delinquent taxes, and a $21 deed filing fee is due at checkout.
  • Deeds usually arrive about 120 days after the sale, and the county is not responsible for evicting occupants.

Each month's delinquent amount holds if paid by 5 p.m. on the 20th, and interest accrues afterward. Unrelated to land, unpaid personal property tax blocks vehicle tag renewal, and a court warrant can follow if it remains unpaid by October 20.

A deed goes to the Register of Deeds together with a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire. The County Clerk then logs the transfer for tax purposes and keeps the owner's mailing address on the tax system.

Which deed form fits your sale is a question for a real estate attorney or title company. Phone numbers: Register of Deeds 316-660-9400, County Clerk 316-660-9200, Treasurer 316-660-9000.

Ask the County Clerk or your city clerk about special assessments before closing. Those are tracked apart from the general levy.

sections.h2: Which Sedgwick County sellers run into trouble?
sections.html:
The most urgent cases are houses with several years of unpaid tax, because the foreclosure clock runs on the two and a half and three and a half year marks. Inherited houses come next, since heirs are among those who may redeem. And owners who miss the 30-day informal appeal window have less room that year, because a value can be appealed only once.

  • Get the delinquent balance from the Treasurer before you set a price.
  • Find out whether special assessments are attached to the parcel.
  • Decide early whether to appeal the notice, because the appeal is limited to one per tax year.

To talk through a sale, send the address of your Sedgwick County house and we will describe what a cash offer could involve.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with a tax problem
sections.html:
1. Phone the Treasurer, 316-660-9000, for the delinquent balance with interest and fees.
  2. Ask if a foreclosure case is on file in District Court, since that changes the redemption terms.
  3. Ask about special assessments at the County Clerk, 316-660-9200, or at your city clerk.
  4. Pick a buyer and a title company. At closing the title company pays the tax balance from the proceeds, and that payment in full is what ends the matter.
  5. Record the deed and the Sales Validation Questionnaire with the Register of Deeds, 316-660-9400.

A large balance makes timing critical. Payment in full halts foreclosure and a new deed alone does not, so schedule the closing to pay what is owed ahead of the day before the auction. Keep copies of the payoff letter and the closing statement. If a buyer asks later about the lien or the case, those papers answer it. A seller who has them can also show clearly that the county's claim was paid in full on a specific date.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal a Sedgwick County property valuation?
faqs.a: Begin at the Sedgwick County Appraiser's Office. The form on the back of your March 1 notice is due within 30 days, usually March 31.

faqs.q: When is Sedgwick County property tax due?
faqs.a: Statements arrive by December 15. Pay everything or the first half by December 20, then the second half by May 10.

faqs.q: How long can taxes go unpaid before foreclosure in Sedgwick County?
faqs.a: Parcels two and a half or three and a half years behind are selected. If nobody redeems, a District Court case leads to auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Sedgwick County house if taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes. A closing that pays the balance in full halts foreclosure. A recorded deed by itself does not.

faqs.q: What forms are filed when a Sedgwick County house sells?
faqs.a: The deed and a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire go to the Register of Deeds, and then the County Clerk updates the tax record.
